answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging every identity a small, non-transferable proof of useful work that cannot be copied: each agent must periodically process a unique slice of real network data and publish a verifiable result, like shale layers that only form under real pressure over time. A tide of cheap clones drowns because each copy must do its own distinct work, and the cost of faking a thousand slices exceeds any reward, while basalt-hard audit trails let peers check every claim without trusting the claimant.
